crew.command_module_pilot: Richard F. Gordon Jr. (remained in lunar orbit aboard Yankee Clipper)

landing_coordinates.landing_accuracy: First pinpoint lunar landing in human history, touching down within 163m of Surveyor 3

propulsion_system.propellants: Aerozine 50 fuel and Nitrogen Tetroxide (N2O4) oxidizer, hypergolic
propulsion_system.combustion_chamber: Ablative-cooled thrust chamber with columbium radiation-cooled nozzle extension

equipment_stowage_and_discarded_hardware.quad_1: Manned Flight Awareness commemorative plaque, ladder, descent engine
equipment_stowage_and_discarded_hardware.quad_2: Modular Equipment Stowage Assembly (MESA) containing lunar surface TV camera, rock sample collection boxes, core tubes, Apollo lunar hand tools
equipment_stowage_and_discarded_hardware.quad_3: Scientific equipment bay, Solar Wind Composition foil experiment
equipment_stowage_and_discarded_hardware.quad_4: ALSEP stowage subpackages 1 and 2, SNAP-27 graphite fuel cask assembly mounted externally on quadrant corner

artifacts_currently_at_site: Intrepid Descent Stage structure, tanks, landing gear, and DPS engine bell
Egress ladder and commemorative stainless steel plaque
Jettisoned PLSS backpacks (Conrad and Bean) on surface below hatch
Jettisoned lunar overshoes, gloves, armbands, and waste bags
Apollo Lunar Hand Tool Carrier and discarded sampling scoops/tongs
United States Flag (planted ~7m south of LM)
SNAP-27 graphite transport cask (attached to Quad 4 frame)
Lunar surface sensing probes (broken and bent under footpads)
